title: Founder pilot + pricing play (scratchpad)
content:
Context / objective:
- Quick personal scratchpad for outreach to founders / early execs when proposing a small evangelist pilot (4-6 weeks) focused on latency/cost improvements for chat/agent workloads.
- Goal: get commitment to a short, scoped pilot (POC contract, NDA if needed) that surfaces measurable ROI (latency p50/p95, $/1M tokens) and a product testimonial.
- Primary target: founders/CTO of mid-stage infra/consumer SaaS with chat or agent features (10–150 engineers, $2M–$50M ARR).
- Keep messaging founder-friendly: efficiency, speed to product improvement, low operational lift.

Quick prospect snapshot: ArborTech (example)
- What they do: SMB-focused field ops platform that added a conversational assistant for dispatch and customer responses.
- Trigger signals: recent Series B (Sept 2025), hiring for ML infra, job posting for Sr. ML Engineer.
- Likely decision-makers: CTO (Samir Khan), Head of Product (Maya Lin), ML Eng lead (Diego Ortiz).
- Technical environment (guess): AWS EKS, huggingface-backed models for prototyping, early attempts at caching.

Why Redwood matters to them (short hooks):
- Cut token spend and per-request latency by 40–60% via batching + prefix/KV caching and quantization on compatible model variants.
- Single API to stage from prototype -> dedicated capacity -> private deploy without rewriting product code.
- Measurable SLA improvements for time-sensitive user flows (dispatch responses, SLA-based notifications).

Pilot framing / scope (recommended):
- Duration: 4 weeks (kickoff + 3 quick sprints)
- Success metrics: p50 latency reduction >30%, p95 < target (e.g., <600ms for short queries), effective token $/1000 reduction >= 30%, no degradation in fidelity on core prompts (measured by n=50 prompt set).
- Deliverables: integration PoC, dashboard of metrics in Redwood Console, recommended config for caching/batching/quantization, short writeup + 1 live demo.
- Minimal ops required by customer: a single E2E integration engineer (or product engineer) to wire a route and test prompts.
- Redwood commitments: 2 SRE/solutions hours per week + engineering ramp hour(s) + a single pilot pricing credit line.

Pilot pricing anchors (three quick options):
1) Free trial credit + success fee: $0 upfront (hosted), payable success fee $7k on completion if metrics hit. Good for product-first founders who hate up-front spend.
2) Discounted pilot contract: 1-month committed spend $10k (50% discount on list). Includes dedicated time and prioritized support.
3) Revenue-share / performance bonus: base $2k + $X per % latency improvement beyond baseline. (Harder to sell, creative for cost-sensitive ops teams.)

Email templates (short / cold):
- Short variant (subject: 4-week pilot to cut chat costs for ArborTech)
Hi Samir — quick note. We help teams like yours cut per-request latency and token cost for production chat/agent features without re-architecting the product. Would you be open to a 4‑week pilot where we aim to reduce p50 latency by 30% and token spend by ~40%? No heavy infra changes — we integrate via your existing API route and run caching/batching/quantization configs. Small ask: 1 engineer & 20–30 sample prompts.
If that sounds reasonable I can send a one‑page scope and pricing options.
— Asha

- Long variant (for warm inbound):
Hey Maya — following up on our intro from Priya. Based on what you shared about the conversational assistant, we can: (1) run a 4‑week pilot to measure real latency and cost wins using your top 50 prompts; (2) deliver a Redwood Console dashboard that shows p50/p95, per-route token $ and a recommended config you can roll to prod. We’d staff a solutions engineer and require one engineer full-time 10–20 hours/week for wiring. Two pricing options: fully sponsored pilot or a discounted committed pilot. Happy to outline both in a one-pager.

Call script bullets (15–20 min intro):
- 0–3m: quick intros, confirm role/ownership of chat stack.
- 3–6m: confirm the user-facing flow (examples, volumes, targets). Ask: what is acceptable p95? current pain?
- 6–10m: share quick wins we've driven (e.g., cut token cost 35% for ecom assistant, p95 improvement 400ms) — keep concrete numbers.
- 10–15m: propose pilot framing + logistics, pricing anchors, next step = kickoff + short NDA/POC doc.
- Close ask: can we put a kickoff on calendar next week?

Objection handling (cheat sheet):
- "We already have in-house infra / can tune the model": acknowledge, then pivot: tuning helps but serving/runtime + batching/caching yield a separate class of wins — and we can run a side-by-side with no code rewrite. Offer a 1-week smoke test to show delta.
- "We can't sign another vendor / procurement is slow": offer a limited scoped MSA addendum + pilot legal-lite (SOW + simple NDA). Emphasize credits to start.
- "Latency matters less than accuracy": agree and propose guardrails: we include a fidelity checklist (50 prompts evaluated blind) and will rollback configs that hurt scores.
- "Pricing is unknown / cost could escalate": anchor with per-month pilot cap and telemetry alerts in the Console. We can set hard token caps.

Open questions / assumptions to validate early:
- exact model(s) they're running in prod or staging (gpt-like, Llama-family, custom).
- average prompt length, typical session structure (prefix length, streaming vs non-streaming).
- whether they have PII/regulated data that would push private deploy.
- expected monthly token volume (helps recommend dedicated vs hosted).

Artifacts to prep before outreach:
- 1‑pager pilot scope template (customizable) — TODO: draft v0 and PR to pilot-materials repo.
- 2–3 anonymized case studies with numbers (need permission).
- A concise checklist for customer's side (one page).
- Short demo script + sample dashboard screenshots for Redwood Console.

Next steps (my TODOs):
- Draft pilot scope 1-pager and hand to Priya for review (target 2026-03-08).
- Pull ArborTech financings/hiring signals and drop into short prospect doc (Tom).
- Create Slack thread #founder-pilot-play and add Tom/Priya.
- Prepare one cold-email A/B test: short vs product-hook heavy.

Notes to self / heuristics:
- Founders like experiments framed as "try this for 4 weeks; we’ll prove it with numbers".
- Avoid long product decks on first contact — founders respond to specific, measurable outcomes.
- When in doubt, offer speed (kickoff within 7 days) over bigger discounts.

Rough timeline for a 4-week pilot:
- Week 0: kickoff, data access, routes wired (dev sync).
- Week 1: baseline metrics collection + initial config testing.
- Week 2: iterative tuning (caching, batch sizes, quantization sampling).
- Week 3: stability, guardrail tests, fidelity checks.
- Week 4: closeout, metrics report, recommended rollout plan.

End of scratchpad. Notes likely messy — will clean into one-pager after priya/tom sync.
